newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold, platinum futures rise on yen's slip.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold, platinum futures rise on yen's slip.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo gold and platinum futures ended higher across the board in buoyant trade on Tuesday, hauled up by the yen's further dip against the dollar, traders said.
Newly listed benchmark October gold ended at 1,390 yen, while others ranged from three to nine yen per gram higher.
Newly listed benchmark October platinum settled at 1,396 yen, after rising to 1,403 yen during the day. Others ranged from four to seven yen higher.
Traders said they were taking bullish views on yen-based futures, backed by a perception the yen has more room to slip.
The dollar hit a new 42-month high of 114.92 yen in Tokyo on Tuesday.
Bullion was quoted at $382.85/383.15 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against 382.90/383.40 in New York on Monday.
Private investors carried out fresh buying in distant months after liquidating their longs in nearbys. But prices retreated from early highs, succumbing to profit-taking later in the day.
In bullion market, gold drifted sideways around $383.00 per ounce during Asian hours.
Traders said the gold market reacted little to sharp falls in Japan's gold imports in September.
Palladium futures settled narrowly mixed. Weak Japanese physical demand and the easier spot palladium prices discouraged interest in palladium futures.
Japan's September palladium imports totalled 4.15 tonnes, down 42.2 percent from a year earlier, according to Finance Ministry data released on Tuesday.

"Japan's palladium market faces an oversupply trend. Efforts by Japan's electronic manufactures to substitute palladium with cheaper metals like nickel are also reducing fresh palladium demand," one bullion house official said.
